changes: p2: 'vālāvatmahāvihāre [ʼ]vasthita' means 'residing in' the vihāra, so it is now given as residence as well as affiliation
p1: evidence widened to include 'lalikaśrīvajradaguviracitā'; the name is still read as Vajradatta, the known author of the Lokeśvaraśataka
Notes now cover the unclear 'lalikaśrī' and the uncertain identity of the vihāra

notes: The author's name 'vajradagu' is probably a corruption of Vajradatta, the traditional author of the Lokeśvaraśataka. The preceding 'lalikaśrī' is unclear: it may be a corrupt epithet or part of the author's name. The scribe's name has a lacuna after Ratnapati ('ratnapati++vāsaṃ'), so there may be more of the name or a word like 'nivāsa'. The vihāra 'vālāvat' is not securely identified, so the place is not normalized. The colophon gives no date.
